problem_keywords: reconciler cursor advances past abandoned candidate
propositions: An unvoted change stalls indefinitely because the reconciler advances its cursor past abandoned candidates whose reviews timeout or error, permanently excluding them from future windows via the server-side ?t1= filter.

The reconciler cursor is an unconditional high-water mark (newest event time) rather than a low-water mark; it should persist the minimum of newest_event and the oldest retryably abandoned candidate to re-admit failed reviews.
When a webhook delivery fails and a review times out or errors, the change is not retried on the next reconciler pass; it vanishes from the scanned candidate set forever.
The Gerrit webhooks plugin delivers at-most-once (not at-least-once), discarding events after maxTries and on container recreation, making the reconciler the only recovery path.

A change can be revived by emitting a new events-log event with a timestamp after the cursor (via recheck-review comment or no-op rebase), confirming the original upload event was dropped by the reconciler.
Observable queue depth and held-back candidate tracking are absent, making it impossible to distinguish a queued change from a dropped one.
